account:
Today has seemed mostly routine. I made my market visit, had lunch at home, reviewed the town accounts, attended tea, and returned to the office. The treasury held 128 emeralds when I checked it, and I left them untouched. The baker put bread into the market stall, and the neighbour reported that the baker was stocking fresh bread and the innkeeper was tending supplies. Those sound like ordinary provisioning, not evidence of any special event.

The only unusual news is an unconfirmed rumour of a celebration or changes to the bridge. The neighbour had seen no evidence, and said the baker knew of no celebration. I do not know who started the rumours or what, if anything, they concern. I also noticed a lantern appear by a great-hall table this morning; I did not see who placed it or learn why, so I cannot connect it to the rumours.

The secretary spent time verifying the location of my tea appointment, initially without success. At tea the neighbour directly confirmed that the cottage at (16, -60, 105) is the place for tea at three every day. This appears to have been ordinary schedule coordination. The secretary has now returned to my office and asked whether there is correspondence or other business to handle before I go home at seven. No specific urgent town problem has been brought to my attention. Tomorrow's known business includes the morning mill grain inspection and afternoon council letters.
